projects.title: Selected projects
projects.fit: Have a service you want to bring to mobile? A product that is missing an app? Or an idea where you need to find the right first step? These are the kinds of briefs I have worked on.

domov.title: Domov pod palcem
domov.tagline: Smart-home control for iOS and Android
domov.problem: The owner of a smart home wanted to control lighting, blinds, gates, heating, heat recovery and air conditioning from one place – without switching between each manufacturer's app.
domov.delivered: I delivered a mobile app that configures itself for the household after sign-in and talks to it over a secured connection. Schedules for heating and other devices are included.
domov.decision: Every control sits within reach of the thumb of the hand holding the phone, so the home can be operated comfortably one-handed – with the shopping in the other.
domov.result: The delivered app covers complete control of the home, including scheduled modes.

stable.title: Smart Stable
stable.tagline: Operations app for a stable manager
stable.problem: The manager of a cattle stable needed an overview of the conditions inside and a way to control the equipment even when not on site.
stable.delivered: I delivered an iOS and Android app in which the manager controls fans, side tarpaulins and lighting, watches live sensor readings – temperature, humidity and CO₂ – and their last 24 hours in charts.
stable.decision: The app watches for undesirable conditions on its own. When readings drift or a device reports a fault, the manager gets a push notification instead of having to watch the screen.
stable.result: The app supports several stables of one operator and adapts to the signed-in user's permissions.

studanky.title: Studánky
studanky.tagline: An app for monitoring natural springs
studanky.problem: Hikers and locals have no reliable way to know which natural springs are flowing right now and whether the water is fine.
studanky.delivered: For the Studánky project I am developing a mobile app for monitoring the state of natural springs and planning trips. Users find springs on a map, scan a QR code at the spring and add the current state through a short questionnaire.
studanky.decision: Data collection relies on the people at the spring: a report takes a few taps, and damage can be reported directly to the spring's caretaker.
studanky.result: The app is in development. I keep adding springs and features.

process.title: We start with your goal, not with an app.
process.intro: First I need to understand what you do, where you're heading and what's missing today. We agree every next step in advance – what I'll do, what you'll get and what it will cost.

free.title: Free introductory consultation
free.text: Usually 60–90 minutes, in person or online. We go through your business, goals and the main open questions. You leave with a summary and a proposed next step.

entries.situation: You don't know whether to build, or what
entries.start: We start with stage 1: the decision.

entries.situation: You know exactly what you want
entries.start: We start with stage 2: designing the full version.

entries.situation: You want to test the idea first
entries.start: We start with stage 2: designing a first version.
I assess it and we continue with stage 4.

stages.title: Decision: does a digital product make sense?
stages.text: I map your goals, users and market, review competitors and existing solutions, and prepare options – from an off-the-shelf tool to a product of your own. I'll recommend what makes sense, even if that's “don't build yet”.
outputs: A summary of goals and needs
Options with a recommendation and a rough estimate

stages.title: Design: what exactly to build
stages.text: We settle the scope – the full version, or first a version with just the essentials (an MVP). I design the key screens and flows and refine them with your feedback before I start coding.

stages.title: Development and launch
stages.text: I build in increments and show you finished work along the way so you can react. I test the product and release it to the App Store and Google Play, or to the web. A first version tests a specific use case – it does not guarantee demand or revenue.
outputs: A working product for iOS and Android, or the web
Administration and integrations with your systems as needed

stages.title: Operation and growth
stages.text: After launch I take care of operation, updates and fixes. We plan further versions from real usage – step by step, the first version becomes a complete product that grows with your business.

process.scope: Most often I build mobile apps for iOS and Android. As needed, I add a web administration, a server and integrations with your systems – or a web app, if that makes more sense.
process.handover: After each stage you decide whether to continue. You don't have to commit to the whole journey up front.

about.title: One person. A team of AI agents.
bio: I'm Jakub Smolík. For more than six years I have been designing and developing mobile apps – for banks, the public sector and large companies, where security and reliability matter. For founders and businesses I build products of their own, for example in agriculture or smart homes. Technology is a tool for me, not the goal: what interests me is what the product will bring you.

I don't join other companies' teams as one more developer by the hour. I take on products I can be responsible for as a whole – from the first idea to the next versions. I'm based in Prague and happy to come to a meeting.

ai.title: How I work with AI agents
ai.workspaceAlt: Jakub Smolík at work at a desk with a monitor and a laptop
paragraphs: Time-consuming work – research, drafts, prototypes, coding, tests and documentation – I do together with a team of AI agents. That lets me handle a scope that would otherwise need a small team, faster and without agency overhead. Decisions, review and responsibility for the result stay with me.

Your data stays protected. I do general work with large cloud AI models; anything that contains your sensitive data or know-how I process with local models on my own computer, so that information never leaves it. We agree at the start what counts as sensitive.
Hence the name smolikja team: me and my team of AI agents.

assurances.title: What you can count on

items.title: The product is yours
items.text: I hand over the code at agreed milestones, or it lives in your repository from the start. You own the App Store and Google Play accounts and the production servers – I'm happy to help set them up.

items.title: Someone else can pick it up
items.text: I use mainstream technologies and every project has detailed documentation. If our collaboration ends, I hand the project over properly.

items.title: Schedules with a buffer
items.text: I plan with room for the unexpected. I announce holidays in advance and we adjust the plan, so you always know where things stand.

assurances.note: We set out the details in the contract for your project.

items.question: Do I need a finished brief?
items.answer: No. The introductory consultation is free and is there for me to understand your situation and goals. More detailed research, analysis and solution design I price according to the agreed scope. I start paid work only once you approve it.

items.question: Why one person and not an agency?
items.answer: You talk directly to the person who designs and builds the product – nothing gets lost in handoffs, and one person is accountable for the result. AI agents give me the capacity of a small team, so I can do more in less time and without agency overhead. If your product needed many people working in parallel from day one, I'll tell you.

items.question: How much does it cost?
items.answer: The price depends on what the product should do and which systems it connects to. After the introductory consultation I propose the next steps. For a clearly defined brief I offer a fixed price; for incremental development we agree a budget and priorities.

items.question: How long does a first version take?
items.answer: It depends on its scope and the systems it connects to. I give a timeline estimate once it's clear what the first version should do – usually after the introductory consultation or after clarifying the brief.

items.question: What if you're not available?
items.answer: I plan schedules with a buffer so there is room for the unexpected, and I always let you know where things stand. I announce holidays in advance. You hold the code, documentation and accounts, so another developer can pick up the project at any time. We write the specific rules into the contract.

items.question: How do you use AI, and what happens to my data?
items.answer: AI agents help me with research, drafts, code, tests and documentation; I make the decisions and review the work. Sensitive data and know-how I process only with local models on my own computer – I don't send them to cloud AI tools. We agree at the start what you consider sensitive, and if you like, we sign a non-disclosure agreement.

items.question: What happens after launch?
items.answer: We agree maintenance and further development based on what real usage shows. I plan changes by priority and the agreed budget – it's a clear agreement, not unlimited support.

items.question: Can you take over an existing app?
items.answer: Yes. First I assess the existing app and propose the best next step. A rewrite from scratch is not the default recommendation.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: This page describes which personal data I process on smolikja.team, for what purpose and what rights you have.

sections.title: Who processes the data
paragraphs: The data controller is {operator}. For anything concerning personal data, contact me at {email}.

sections.title: Contact form
paragraphs: When you write to me through the form, I process your name, e-mail address and the text of your message. The purpose is to answer your enquiry and arrange a possible collaboration; the legal basis is pre-contractual negotiation and my legitimate interest in handling the enquiry.

The message is delivered to my mailbox by Resend (Resend, Inc., USA) acting as a processor. I keep the data for as long as needed to handle the enquiry and any resulting collaboration, then delete it.
To protect the form from abuse I briefly keep a hash of the sender's IP address; it expires after 24 hours at most.

sections.title: Cookies and analytics
paragraphs: The site uses no analytics or marketing cookies and does not track your behaviour. It stores a single technical cookie, NEXT_LOCALE, with the language you chose, valid for one year.

sections.title: Your rights
paragraphs: You have the right to access your data, to have it corrected or erased, to restrict processing and to object. Just write to the e-mail above. You can also lodge a complaint with the Czech Office for Personal Data Protection.
